title: manuscript-guard reporting checklist
description: A reporting guideline's item list, as published. These are retrieved from the guideline's own site and recorded with their source, never written from memory: a checklist whose items are approximately right is worse than no checklist, because it produces confident coverage of the wrong things.

source_file.description: The official document the items were transcribed from, stored under profiles/reporting/sources/. Present so a reader can check the transcription against the original, exactly as a literature quote can be checked against its source.

applies_to.description: The study designs this checklist covers, in the guideline's own words.

kind.description: What kind of instrument this is, where it is not a reporting guideline. "scale" means an appraisal instrument whose items are what an editor or a reviewer scores, as SANRA's are: the submission pack then presents it as a scale rather than as a completed reporting checklist, which is a different claim. Absent or empty for every reporting guideline.

verification.description: How thoroughly the transcription was checked against the source. Recorded because it differs: a Word table allows every item's full text to be verified, a column-laid-out PDF allows only each item's opening clause, and a rating scale read line by line allows no independent check at all — what it offers instead is the rules it reads by, which `reporting/scale.py` states, with the cases they produce pinned in tests. The three should not be mistaken for the same guarantee.

id.description: The guideline's own item number, e.g. 6a.

applies_to.description: Study designs this item is restricted to, where the checklist says so (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional).

clarification.description: The line a scale prints under an item's title to clarify it, where the form has one — SANRA items 5 and 6 carry "(e.g., ...)". Kept apart from the options so the pack can print the item as the form does.

options.description: A scale item's scored options, in the order the form prints them. The item's text joins them for a reader of the profile; these are the parts, each as published.
